assets.originalPrompt: Use case: photorealistic-natural. Asset type: production game terrain ALBEDO / BASE COLOR texture, one single square 2048x2048 image, not a scene or a presentation. Primary request: create an exceptionally detailed seamless tileable neutral meadow ground microdetail texture to replace cheap procedural noise in a third-person survival game. Orthographic view straight down of about 2.6 by 2.6 meters of dense short meadow grass mixed with dry fine grass fibres, organic compact earth, tiny irregular mineral grains and small areas of flattened grass. Fine overlapping thin blades in varied directions, broken natural clusters, irregular small-scale detail, evenly distributed. Materials must read convincingly from up close without appearing as a repeating carpet, coarse rope, or random white noise. Color palette: bright low-saturation warm greige and neutral silver-grey, nearly monochromatic, since the game's vertex colors will tint this image green for meadows, tan for beaches and grey for rock. Preserve luminance mainly 0.70 to 0.95, restrained contrast and sparse slightly darker pores. This is neutral color modulation, not a vivid green grass photograph. Composition: fill the entire square edge to edge with homogeneous natural microdetail; no large focal object, no isolated stones, no path or distinctive repeated patch. Lighting: flat perfectly diffuse shadow-free light; no baked sun direction, no perspective, no vignette, no highlights, no ambient cast shadows, no depth of field. Constraints: opposite edges must match exactly for seamless two-axis repeat, no border, no labels, no text, no watermark, no texture atlas, no material sphere, no collage, no rendered 3D object. Deliver only the texture image.
assets.refinementPrompt: Edit target: the attached generated game terrain base-color texture. Keep the square edge-to-edge top-down texture composition and the neutral low-saturation greige color palette. Change only the material structure: remove almost all long tangled straw and prominent thin grass strands. Replace with fine compact mineral soil, tiny irregular sub-centimeter grit, scattered minute weathered pebbles, subtle moss-like fine organic grain and very sparse short broken root fragments. It should be a versatile neutral ground detail texture that can be tinted as grass, beach sand, dry dirt or stone in a game. Make it brighter and lower contrast: diffuse neutral pale warm grey, most areas luminance about 0.78-0.92, some shallow pores about 0.64; no large dark patches or bright white speckles. Rich microdetail at 2048x2048. Opposite edges must match exactly for seamless two-axis repetition. Perfectly flat diffuse illumination, no directionally lit lumps or baked shadows, no perspective, no border, no text, no atlas, no presentation. Deliver just one square albedo texture.

assets.prompt: Use case: photorealistic-natural. Asset type: production game ALBEDO / BASE COLOR material texture, one square 2048x2048 image only. Create a seamlessly tileable neutral pale wood grain texture for rifle stocks, doors and crates in a third-person survival game. Orthographic flat close-up of a single continuous solid wood surface, not planks. Grain direction horizontal left-to-right throughout. Convincing fine wood pores and silky irregular elongated fibres, subtle flowing growth lines, restrained weathering, small fine scratches, slight grain density variation, no dominant knots and no large cracks. Neutral very low-saturation light warm-grey and pale beige; fairly bright 0.75-0.95 luminance with low to moderate contrast so existing game vertex colors can tint it walnut or oak. Avoid a vivid orange/brown color, strong striping or glossy wood. Opposite left/right and top/bottom edges must match seamlessly. Flat shadow-free diffuse lighting, no baked directional lighting or highlights, no perspective, no vignette, no plank borders, no panels, no text, no watermark, no material sphere, no collage. Full-bleed texture only.

notes: These are generated albedo images; the current materials retain subtle procedural normals. Inspect tiling in-engine before treating AI output as exactly seamless.
